# Human-time ledger

We track *human* time on this project, per the contribution norm: reading code,
thinking about the math/proof, interacting with agents, and reviewing — and
**excluding** environment setup, learning the codebase, and general software /
infrastructure work. Pull requests self-report it via the **Human time spent**
field in the PR template; a GitHub Action nudges submitters who forget.

> Why self-reported and not measured: in an agent-heavy workflow, wall-clock
> decouples from human-active-time (agents run for tens of minutes; some runs are
> overnight). Commit-timestamp wall-clock therefore badly over-counts. Only the
> human knows their active engagement, so we ask.

## Baseline

- **Project through 2026-06-06: ≈ 12 h** of active human time — the
  mathematician-user's directing: scope, the axiom-vs-proof boundary, hack-blocker
  and faithfulness judgments, and review of every landing. (The Lean was
  agent-written; zero human-written Lean.) Self-estimate, approximate.

## Ongoing

From 2026-06-06, per-PR human-time estimates accumulate from the baseline above —
read them off the merged PRs' **Human time spent** fields.
